Definition: from G5104 and G1063 and G3767; truly for then, i.e. consequently:--there-(where-)fore.
BiblicalUsage: Therefore — the word that turns a promise into a conclusion. Paul says the one who despises the command despises not man but God, and Hebrews says, seeing we are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight and run the race.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word does real work: it joins what God has done to what we must do next.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
